 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-owner of the offending Lorry bearing No.KA-41/751, calling in question the judgment and award dated 19.11.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.479/2013, on the file of the Nagaraj vs Smt Manjula on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84193915/
2 Senior Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. And Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sagar, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) questioning the liability fastened on him.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. And Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts:
2. On 31.12.2012 morning, Yogendra, the husband of the first claimant and father of claimant Nos.2 and 3 was going in a Lorry bearing registration No.KA- 41/751 as a Loader from Yedehalli to Gamanagadde.

The first respondent being the driver had driven the said Lorry in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident near Gamanagadde cross,
Kalluhalla bridge.
Due to the impact, the husband of the first claimant sustained grievous injury and succumbed to injuries on in the spot.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record allowed the petition in part and awarded a compensation of Rs.6,50,000/-,
along with future interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and fastened the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.
The Tribunal had determined the compensation and fastened the liability on the appellant-owner on the ground that the driver of the lorry was not holding the Driving License.
Hence, I.A.No.1/2021 is filed by the appellant-owner seeking to produce the driving license of Sandeep the driver of the offending lorry, by way of additional document.

In order to check the genuinity and veracity and also the period of the Driving License that he was competent to drive the said vehicle, the additional documents are to be considered at the time of leading evidence.
Therefore, for the reasons stated in the application, I.A. No.2/2021 is allowed.

6. Therefore, the case is remanded to the Tribunal without expressing any opinion on merits involved in the case, to consider whether the driver of the offending lorry was holding a valid Driving License to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
All the contentions are kept open.
The parties are given liberty to adduce any evidence if they are so advised.

7. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is Allowed and Remanded.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 19.11.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.479/2013, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. And Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sagar is set-aside.
iii.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & J.M.F.C. And Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The matter is remanded to the Tribunal.
The parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 01.03.2023, without expecting any further notice in this regard.
The Tribunal shall consider the matter afresh and dispose of the same within six months from 01.03.2023, in accordance with law.
